Brand Guidelines · Final
The complete reference for using the Moto Italia identity correctly and consistently — logo, colour, typography, and application, across every touchpoint from the storefront to social media.
Prepared by Wecomeone for Motoitalia Confidential · August 2026
Introduction
The Mark
The Moto Italia identity is built on two elements: a bold, confident wordmark, and the Italian tricolore rendered as three angled bars — a direct nod to the heritage of Piaggio, Vespa, Moto Guzzi, and Aprilia, and the Italian craftsmanship behind every brand in the store. The forward lean of the bars suggests motion without relying on literal imagery. It is deliberately simple, so it scales cleanly from a storefront sign down to a social media avatar.
01 — The Logo
Primary Lockup
Three approved colour versions, produced from the final vector artwork. Always use these master files — never recreate, redraw, or approximate the logo.
Primary — On White
Default version. Use on white or light backgrounds — website, documents, print.
On Brand Red
For merchandise, packaging, and promotional material where a bold red field is used. Bars fade white to soft pink for contrast on red.
Reversed — On Black
For dark backgrounds — website hero sections, social media, signage at night.
The Icon Mark
Standalone Symbol
The tricolore bars can be used alone as a compact mark for favicons, social avatars, and small-format applications where the full wordmark will not fit legibly. Three approved colour versions:
Icon — On White
Icon — On Red
Icon — On Black
02 — Clear Space & Minimum Size
Give It Room
The logo needs breathing room to stay legible and keep its impact. Never let text, imagery, or the edge of a layout crowd it.
Minimum clear space on all sides = the height of the icon mark ("x"). Nothing else should sit inside this zone.
Minimum Size
Don't Go Smaller
Below these sizes the wordmark loses legibility. Use the icon mark alone instead of shrinking the full lockup further.
Digital minimum — 280px wide
Absolute minimum — 120px wide
Icon only — below 120px, use this instead
03 — Colour Palette
Rosso, Nero, Bianco, Verde
A tight, confident palette drawn directly from the final logo artwork and the Italian tricolore. Red carries the brand — use it deliberately, not everywhere.
Rosso
HEX #DF0123
RGB 223, 1, 35
CMYK 0, 100, 84, 13
Primary brand colour. Wordmark, key CTAs, accents. Use with intent — it's the loudest colour in the system.
Nero
HEX #0D0D0D
RGB 13, 13, 13
CMYK 0, 0, 0, 95
Primary background for digital. Signage, apparel, website base colour.
Bianco
HEX #F5F3EF
RGB 245, 243, 239
CMYK 0, 1, 2, 4
Primary light background. Print, documents, light-mode digital surfaces. Warm off-white, not pure white.
Verde
HEX #069147
RGB 6, 145, 71
CMYK 79, 0, 78, 24
Tricolore accent only. Never used as a dominant colour — appears exclusively within the logo bars.
Usage Ratio
As a rough guide: Nero and Bianco should make up the majority of any layout (backgrounds, body text), Rosso carries emphasis and calls to action, and Verde stays inside the logo mark — it is not a general-purpose brand colour.
04 — Typography
Type System
The wordmark uses a bold, geometric sans-serif set in tight letter-spacing. For everything else — website, documents, social captions — the system below keeps that same confident, modern character.
Display — Headlines
Bebas Neue
RIDE ITALIAN. RIDE MOTO ITALIA.
Use for large headlines, section titles, and callouts. Always set in uppercase. Free on Google Fonts.
Body — Text & UI
Inter Semibold — for subheadings and emphasis
Inter Regular — for body copy, paragraphs, product descriptions, and everyday website and document text. Clean, highly legible at small sizes, and pairs cleanly with the boldness of Bebas Neue without competing for attention.
Weights used: Light (300) for large body text, Regular (400) for standard copy, Semibold (600) for emphasis, Bold (700) sparingly for strong callouts. Free on Google Fonts.

07 — Incorrect Usage
Protect the Mark
Consistency is what makes a brand recognisable. These are the most common ways the logo gets misused — avoid all of them.
✕ Don't Distort
Never stretch, squash, or change the proportions of the logo in any direction.
✕ Don't Recolour
Never apply colours outside the approved palette — including the tricolore bars.
✕ Don't Rotate
The logo always sits level. Never tilt or angle it for effect.
✕ Don't Reduce Contrast
Never place the logo on a busy photo or low-contrast background without a solid holding shape behind it.
✕ Don't Add Effects
No drop shadows, glows, outlines, or 3D effects. The logo is always flat.
✕ Don't Mirror or Reorder
Never flip the logo or change the order of the tricolore bars.
Quick Reference
Summary
✓ Do
Use the master logo files provided — never recreate them
Keep clear space equal to the icon mark's height on all sides
Use the reversed (white) version on dark backgrounds
Use the icon mark alone below 120px width
Keep the tricolore bars in their fixed red-white-green order
✕ Don't
Stretch, squash, or distort the proportions
Recolour the logo outside the approved palette
Rotate or angle the logo for effect
Add drop shadows, glows, or 3D effects
Mirror the logo or reorder the tricolore bars
